data.G: Initial G is the supplied valid baseline (commit 08b3ea3005cc66fadf7e5a4cfce0de6fc541ca12); no research candidate is integrated yet. Assemble and independently confirm the integrated result after the trees report.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the measured baseline takes 0.31093 s on average over three valid samples for n=768, and the supplied row-major code repeats eight-octave noise work per pixel. Three distinct opportunities merit separate trees: reuse of coordinate decomposition across rows and columns, restructuring the scalar Noise/Grad hot path, and SIMD across independent pixels. Do not pursue thread-level parallelism for this one-core target; honor the threads budget. The stated target is AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2, while the available target metadata reports x86_64 and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; exact build flags and effective SIMD features were not independently inspected. The versioned GCC 14.2 Optimize Options manual documents loop vectorization (enabled by default at -O2), but the actual optimization flags are unknown, so measure rather than assume compiler vectorization: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-14.2.0/gcc/Optimize-Options.html. Require each candidate to modify only src/candidate.cpp, preserve correctness and the fixed tolerance for all valid inputs, overwrite the complete output, respect the thread budget, and record failed attempts. Compare candidates only after correctness checks; integrate measured candidates cautiously and independently confirm final G using the separate confirmation seed.

children.objective: Explore scalar reuse of axis coordinate state: for each column and row, compute the eight octave-specific coordinates, floors/lattice indices, fractions and smooth weights once, and share the octave z state. Keep the per-pixel evaluation scalar and avoid SIMD, thread parallelism, and cached output. Preserve coordinate evaluation semantics and test scratch/layout overhead as well as runtime. Validate n=768 and smaller/shifted-bound checks against the fixed tolerance, and record failed layouts or approaches.
children.subject: Per-axis, per-octave coordinate-state reuse

children.objective: Starting from the scalar kernel, restructure the per-pixel Noise/Grad hot path to reduce corner-hash and gradient-selection overhead; separately measure equivalent interpolation/polynomial forms and fixed-octave control-flow changes. Do not add axis precomputation, SIMD, or thread parallelism so the result isolates scalar-kernel changes. Keep every transformation within the fixed tolerance for all valid inputs; run the full correctness checks and record failed attempts.
children.subject: Scalar Perlin hash, gradient, and interpolation kernel

children.objective: Explore explicit SIMD across adjacent independent x pixels on the stated x86 target, including vectorized octave evaluation and efficient permutation-table indexing/gathers. Keep this distinct from axis-state caching and thread parallelism; retain a scalar tail or fallback where needed and use only code accepted by the frozen build and target. Measure end-to-end runtime and validate all specified sizes and shifted bounds against the fixed tolerance; record failed vector widths or implementations.
children.subject: SIMD across independent image pixels
